title: The goal form's risk class becomes a policy tier, and the live dispatch carries the opt-ins it earns
description:
SPIDR child A of parent task-d56a0cc5f6ae4dc88da5233a9702d9e6 ("One approval, then unattended"), split 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a after measuring the parent at ~20 files across three packages against a 10-file cap. This is the DEPENDENCY LEAF: rows B (Gate 2) and C (Gate 3) both consume the mapping and the carried opt-ins, and both declare dependsOn on this row. Plan and land this FIRST.

OWNER DIRECTION driving the parent (2026-09-09): "we dont want moe-next to be stuck all the time for user approval we can approve the plan at the start but thats it". One human gate at plan/contract time; the rest unattended, with a human ABLE to intervene but not REQUIRED.

MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a. Re-measure before planning; these are the facts this row is scoped against:
- `git grep -n "autoApprovalOptIns" -- packages/** apps/** adapters/**`: the ONLY production caller is apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100 `autoApprovalOptIns: [], riskClassifications: RISK_CLASSIFICATIONS, rules: [],`. Every other hit is a fixture or a .test file. RISK_CLASSIFICATIONS is a local const at :31-36 carrying four `{factId, tier}` entries (R1/R0/R0/R2).
- `git grep -n "AdvisoryRiskClass" -- apps/**`: goal-model.ts:90 `export type AdvisoryRiskClass = "STANDARD" | "ELEVATED" | "RESTRICTED";`, optional field at goal-model.ts:124, set at new-goal-form.tsx:55 and :215. Consumed ONLY at apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts in briefOfDraft as `lines.push(`Risk class: ${draft.riskClass}`)` - a line of PROSE in the brief. No mapping to R0..R3 exists anywhere.
- DEPENDENCY EDGE VERIFIED, no manifest edit needed: apps/control-room/package.json declares `"@moe/core": "workspace:*"`; pnpm-lock.yaml carries the `apps/control-room:` importer at line 70; production code already imports the bare specifier (apps/control-room/src/approvals/approval-gating.ts:4 `} from "@moe/core";`).
- BARREL EXPORTS CONFIRMED at packages/core/src/policy/policy-public.ts: POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS (:40), POLICY_RISK_TIERS (:45), type PolicyRiskTier (:63).
- TYPE-LEVEL FENCE, load-bearing for this row: policy-contract.ts:90-93 `interface PolicyAutoApprovalOptIn { readonly action: string; readonly tier: PolicyAutoApprovalTier }` and :28 `POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS = ["R0","R1"]`. An opt-in CANNOT carry R2 or R3 - the compiler refuses it. So a RESTRICTED goal yields NO opt-in by construction, not by a runtime check this row writes.

OWNER RULING 2026-09-09 on the mapping arithmetic. The parent's DoD asked for set equality both directions between 3 AdvisoryRiskClass values and 4 POLICY_RISK_TIERS, which no total function can satisfy (a 3-set cannot surject onto a 4-set). The owner chose: drop the reachability half, keep totality and injectivity. THE MAPPING IS EXACTLY:
  STANDARD   -> R0  (auto-approvable)
  ELEVATED   -> R1  (auto-approvable)
  RESTRICTED -> R3  (human-only)
R2 is deliberately unreachable from the form. Nothing is weakened: R2 and R3 are both human-only at policy-evaluation.ts:155-158, which returns REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with code HUMAN_ONLY_TIER for both. Do NOT add a fourth advisory class and do NOT widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES, and nothing more. One typed total mapping from AdvisoryRiskClass to PolicyRiskTier, in its own small module under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/. Then live-dispatch-payloads.ts stops passing `autoApprovalOptIns: []` unconditionally: it derives the opt-in list from the goal draft's risk class, emitting opt-ins for the two gate actions ONLY when the mapped tier is in POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS, and an empty list otherwise. The risk class stops being only prose; leave the existing brief line in place (it is advisory text the operator reads) and ADD the typed path beside it.

OUT OF SCOPE, owned by sibling rows - do not touch these files: no daemon change of any kind; no preview or release edge; no decision-record shape; no digest mirror rotation; no MCP allowlist edit; no change to POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS or POLICY_RISK_TIERS.

The action strings the opt-ins name must be MEASURED from the kind constants, not invented: preview-contracts.ts:43 `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND = "preview.decide"` and release-decide-contracts.ts for RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND. Grep them; do not hand-type a literal that drifts.
definitionOfDone: A typed total mapping from AdvisoryRiskClass to PolicyRiskTier exists in one module under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/, with an arm that asserts it is TOTAL (every value in a literal ['STANDARD','ELEVATED','RESTRICTED'] roster maps) and INJECTIVE (three distinct tiers), and pins the three pairs exactly: STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3. The arm iterates a roster declared in the TEST, not the mapping's own keys, so deleting a mapping entry goes RED.

An arm asserts the mapping is closed against the production tier vocabulary: every mapped tier is a member of POLICY_RISK_TIERS imported from the @moe/core bare specifier, and the two auto-approvable results (R0, R1) are members of POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS while R3 is NOT. Assert membership against the imported constants, never against re-typed string literals.

apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts no longer contains the literal `autoApprovalOptIns: []` as an unconditional value; `git grep -n 'autoApprovalOptIns: \[\]' -- apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts` returns no match, quoted in the completion record.

An arm on the live dispatch payload proves the R0/R1 path CARRIES opt-ins: for a draft whose risk class maps to an auto-approvable tier, the emitted slice's autoApprovalOptIns is non-empty and every entry's action equals PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND or RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND read from the daemon kind constants (or a shared re-export), with the mapped tier. Assert the exact action strings and tier, not merely that the array is non-empty.

An arm proves the RESTRICTED path emits an EMPTY opt-in list, and a type-level assertion (expectTypeOf or a ts-expect-error arm) proves an opt-in carrying 'R2' or 'R3' does not compile, pinning the PolicyAutoApprovalTier fence rather than restating it at runtime.

pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test EXITS 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted in the completion record, and the count is NONZERO. An exit-0 leg with no count line is not evidence. pnpm typecheck also exits 0.

No daemon file, no digest mirror, no MCP allowlist file and no packages/core file is modified: `git status --porcelain` at completion shows this row's changes confined to apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/ and apps/control-room/src/live/, quoted in the completion record.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE RESOLUTION BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. NO EDITS.

This row was released once and reclaimed. comment-e41b5b38 records a blocking finding; the plan you are reading RESOLVES it, and the resolution is in approachesConsidered. Read both before touching a file, because the obvious implementation of the row's description is the one that fails.

THE TRAP: `autoApprovalOptIns` is DIGEST INPUT. live-dispatch-payloads.ts:30 `POLICY_REF` is "a known-answer digest of the exact slice below ... which the daemon independently recomputes at install" (:24-27), the slice is at :98-102, and :108 reuses the same ref for `policy.validate`. The header at :29 records the pre-rotation digest and the shape it covered, `{autoApprovalOptIns: [], rules: []}`. So deriving the opt-ins per goal makes the slice variable, and a variable slice cannot carry a hard-coded digest. The daemon refuses at install.

THE RESOLUTION: THREE CONSTANT SLICES, ONE PINNED DIGEST EACH. The mapping is total over three values, so there are at most three possible slices. Nothing varies at runtime except WHICH constant is selected.

CONFIRM THE FACT THE WHOLE DESIGN RESTS ON: `derivePolicySliceDigest` is barrel-exported from `@moe/core` at packages/core/src/policy/policy-public.ts:28, and POLICY_SLICE_DIGEST_VERSION at policy-slice-digest.ts:6 is the same `"moe.policy.slice.content.v1"` the header names. A parity TEST can therefore compute each constant slice's digest and pin it, without pulling crypto into the bundle.
NOTE: I could NOT find an existing parity test — `git grep -ln derivePolicySliceDigest -- 'apps/control-room/**'` returns nothing. You are creating those assertions, not extending one.

CONFIRM THE ACTION-STRING SOURCE, because DoD 4's first branch is impossible: `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` and `RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` live only under apps/daemon/src/, and control-room's manifest declares no daemon dependency. Use RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:106 and :115.

CONFIRM THE TYPE FENCE: `PolicyAutoApprovalOptIn.tier` is `PolicyAutoApprovalTier` and POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS is `["R0","R1"]`. An opt-in cannot carry R2 or R3 — the compiler refuses it. RESTRICTED yields no opt-in BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a runtime check you write.

AND ONE THING TO SETTLE WHILE YOU ARE HERE: the export is named `DEV_PAYLOADS`, while this row's filing calls it "the ONLY production caller" and the test beside it is named `live-dispatch-production.test.ts`. Confirm the table actually reaches a production path. If it turns out to be dev-only, say so on the row — the row still improves the code, but its stated value changes and a grader should hear that from you rather than discover it.
implementationPlan.note:
READ-ONLY STEP. No edits. Five things measured, and one of them changes what steps 3 and 4 build.

1. THE PLAN'S RESOLUTION IS SUPERSEDED, AND I AM NOT BUILDING IT. The plan (submitted 17:11:03Z) resolves the digest conflict with THREE CONSTANT SLICES selected per goal. architect-fa84777a's split-boundary ruling landed at 17:12:12Z, sixty-nine seconds LATER, and rules option (b) instead: ONE constant slice carrying a host-scoped opt-in per gate action, POLICY_REF rotated ONCE. I am following the ruling, for two reasons beyond its being later. First, per-goal opt-ins are the WRONG MODEL: policy-evaluation.ts:161 matches `entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier)`, so the opt-in is host-scoped per ACTION with a tier CEILING, while the goal's risk class is the SUBJECT'S tier and arrives from the folded fact classification. Second, the plan's design is not implementable at this site at all: `payloadFor(kind, aggregateId, version, planningGoalRef)` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:265-268 takes NO draft and no risk class, so there is nothing to select a slice WITH. Three constant slices would need a fourth parameter that no caller has. Confirmed independently against Serena memory decision-auto-approval-optin-is-host-scoped-not-per-goal, which records the same ruling.

2. THE FACT THE DESIGN RESTS ON IS TRUE. `derivePolicySliceDigest` is barrel-exported from @moe/core at policy-public.ts:28, POLICY_SLICE_DIGEST_VERSION is "moe.policy.slice.content.v1" (policy-slice-digest.ts:6), exactly the domain the file header at :24-27 names. It digests only `{autoApprovalOptIns, rules}` plus `riskClassifications` when non-empty, sorted by factId, and EXCLUDES sliceRef to avoid a hash fixed point. It imports node:crypto, so production keeps `import type` only; the test may import the value. There is NO existing parity arm: `git grep -ln derivePolicySliceDigest -- apps/control-room/**` returns nothing and the digest literal appears at exactly ONE site, its own declaration at :30. I am writing the first one.

3. ACTION-STRING SOURCE CONFIRMED, and the shape is not what DoD 4 assumes. RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS is a FLAT tuple of strings, not a record of named constants, so there is no `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` symbol to import anywhere in this package. The daemon constants are genuinely unreachable (apps/* are not workspace libraries). I will bind the two literals with a `satisfies` annotation against RuntimeCommandKind so the COMPILER refuses a kind that leaves the roster, and assert membership in the imported RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS at runtime as well. Both directions, neither hand-typed-and-unchecked.

4. TYPE FENCE CONFIRMED. POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS is ["R0","R1"] (policy-contract.ts:28) and validOptIn refuses anything else at runtime (policy-validation.ts:179-182). R1 is the ceiling and covers subject tiers R0 and R1 by tierRank; R2/R3 are refused earlier at policy-evaluation.ts:151-154 with HUMAN_ONLY_TIER, so RESTRICTED gets no auto-approval by construction on BOTH paths.

5. DEV_PAYLOADS DOES REACH PRODUCTION, and further than the row assumed. Named DEV_ but consumed by live-board.tsx:89 (the render-time dispatchability predicate), live-dispatch.ts:185 (the click path), and activation-port.ts:87, which is the SIX-COMMAND ACTIVATION CHAIN a browser-bootstrapped product runs. It is also consumed by two tests OUTSIDE every per-package filter gate: tests/integration/control-room/live-policy-validation.test.ts sends DEV_PAYLOADS["policy.install"] through the REAL bootstrap handler and asserts ok === true, and dev-payload-parity.test.ts joins it to the daemon's producer. That integration arm is the end-to-end proof of my rotation and I will run it in step 5 on top of the two named gates. Root `pnpm test` and the control-room filter leg are DISJOINT, so both are needed.

TWO THINGS FLAGGED NOW RATHER THAN AT COMPLETION.

DoD 7 CONFINEMENT WILL TAKE A THIRD PATH, and I am declaring it before I write it. apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activation-port.ts:57-58 states in prose: "It GRANTS NOTHING: the slice DEV_PAYLOADS names carries no rules and no auto-approval opt-ins." That sentence becomes FALSE the moment this row lands, and it sits on the activation chain where a reader is most likely to trust it. DoD 7 lists only src/v2/goals/ and src/live/. I intend to correct that comment, and nothing else in that file. It is inside apps/control-room, it is not a daemon file, a digest mirror, an MCP allowlist file or a packages/core file, so every hazard DoD 7 names is still respected. I will quote the porcelain line for it separately in the completion record rather than let a grader discover a third path unannounced. If QA prefers, the alternative is a follow-up bug row and a knowingly false comment shipped in the meantime, which I judge worse.

NO RUNTIME BRANCH ON AN ABSENT RISK CLASS. goal-model.ts:124 makes riskClass optional and the form starts it undefined. The mapping will be TOTAL over the three declared class

implementationPlan.description:
THE MAPPING, IN ITS OWN MODULE (DoD 1, DoD 2).

Create one small module under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/ holding a typed TOTAL mapping from `AdvisoryRiskClass` to `PolicyRiskTier`, importing the tier type and constants from the `@moe/core` BARE specifier. The owner's ruling fixes the pairs exactly:
  STANDARD -> R0, ELEVATED -> R1, RESTRICTED -> R3.
R2 is deliberately unreachable from the form. Do NOT add a fourth advisory class and do NOT widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS.

THE ARMS, and the first has a specific shape requirement (DoD 1): iterate a roster declared IN THE TEST — the literal `["STANDARD","ELEVATED","RESTRICTED"]` — not the mapping's own keys. A test that iterates the mapping shrinks with it, so deleting an entry would stay green. Assert TOTALITY (every roster value maps) and INJECTIVITY (three distinct tiers), and pin the three pairs exactly.

CLOSURE AGAINST THE PRODUCTION VOCABULARY (DoD 2): every mapped tier is a member of POLICY_RISK_TIERS, R0 and R1 are members of POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS, and R3 is NOT. Assert membership against the IMPORTED constants, never against re-typed string literals — a re-typed literal cannot notice the vocabulary moving underneath it.

LEAVE THE PROSE LINE ALONE. live-goal-create.ts:51 pushes `Risk class: ${draft.riskClass}` into the brief; that is advisory text the operator reads. This row ADDS a typed path beside it rather than replacing it.

THREE CONSTANT SLICES, THREE PINNED DIGESTS (live-dispatch-payloads.ts) — the heart of the row.

Replace the single slice with a small CONSTANT TABLE keyed by the mapped tier. Each entry is a slice LITERAL plus its own pinned `sliceRef`:
- RESTRICTED / R3: the EXISTING slice and the EXISTING `POLICY_REF`, byte-for-byte unchanged. Empty opt-ins.
- ELEVATED / R1 and STANDARD / R0: new slice literals carrying opt-ins for the two gate actions at that tier, each with its own pinned digest.

WRITE THEM AS LITERALS. Do not build a slice by spreading a base and inserting a value: the moment a slice is computed its digest stops being a known answer and the daemon refuses at install. Repetition is the point, and a comment should say so, because the next reader's instinct will be to factor it.

THE ACTION STRINGS COME FROM RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (`@moe/contracts`), not from hand-typed literals and not from the daemon.

`policy.validate` AT :108 MUST FOLLOW THE SAME CHOICE. It reuses the ref today; make it carry the digest of whichever slice was selected. A mismatch there is a quieter failure than the install one and the install arm will not catch it.

DoD 3's GREP IS A PROXY FOR "NOT UNCONDITIONAL". An empty opt-in list legitimately survives as the RESTRICTED branch. Quote the grep WITH its surrounding context in the completion record so a grader can see the remaining occurrence is one branch of a table rather than the old unconditional value; if the literal grep must return empty, name the constant rather than contorting the code to hide it.

PIN THE DIGESTS WITH THE PRODUCER, AND PROVE THE PATHS (DoD 4, DoD 5) — in live-dispatch-production.test.ts, which already imports `DEV_PAYLOADS`.

PARITY, the arm that makes the pinned constants trustworthy: for EACH of the three slices, compute its digest with `derivePolicySliceDigest` imported from the `@moe/core` bare specifier and assert it equals the pinned `sliceRef`. This is what lets the production bundle hold constants without hashing anything at runtime. There is no existing parity arm to extend — you are writing the first one, including for the EXISTING POLICY_REF, which is a small bonus this row should bank.

THE R0/R1 PATH CARRIES OPT-INS (DoD 4): for a draft whose risk class maps to an auto-approvable tier, the emitted slice's `autoApprovalOptIns` is non-empty AND every entry's action equals `"preview.decide"` or `"release.decide"` READ FROM RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, with the mapped tier. Assert the exact action strings and the exact tier — "non-empty" alone would pass for an opt-in naming the wrong command.

THE RESTRICTED PATH EMITS AN EMPTY LIST (DoD 5), and the fence is proven at the TYPE level, not restated at runtime: an `expectTypeOf` or `ts-expect-error` arm showing an opt-in carrying `"R2"` or `"R3"` does not compile. Do NOT add a runtime `if (tier === "R3") return []` — the compiler already refuses it, and a runtime check would pass its arm while hiding the fence.

Also assert the selected slice's ref travels to BOTH `policy.install` and `policy.validate` for the same draft, since :108 is the easy one to forget.

GATES AND THE ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 6, DoD 7).

GATES: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` EXIT 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim AND NONZERO — DoD 6 says an exit-0 leg with no count line is not evidence, and it is right: a `--filter` leg prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0, and "0 passed" is exit 0 too. This leg is mandatory and not substitutable, because two mirrors under apps/control-room are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg (epic rail 2). Run `pnpm typecheck` too — this row leans on the type fence, so typecheck is load-bearing evidence here rather than hygiene.

CONFINEMENT PROOF (DoD 7): `git status --porcelain` at completion must show this row's changes confined to apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/ and apps/control-room/src/live/. Quote it. No daemon file, no digest mirror, no MCP allowlist file, no packages/core file. The checkout is SHARED and currently dirty under apps/control-room from a peer row — report only YOUR paths, and never revert or stash a foreign one.

COMPLETION RECORD: state that the digest constraint was resolved by three constant slices rather than by moving the opt-ins out of the slice, so the A/B/C split boundary did NOT move and rows B and C are unaffected. Quote the three parity assertions. Put the arm-by-arm table in a row COMMENT; the completion summary truncates silently at 2000 characters.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: what does the payload builder emit when `draft.riskClass` is UNDEFINED — goal-model.ts:124 makes it optional and new-goal-form.tsx:55 starts it undefined, so which slice does a goal with no risk class install, and is that the SAFE one? Can a slice ever be selected whose pinned ref belongs to a different slice, and what catches that besides the parity arm? If someone later adds a fourth advisory class, what fails first — a compile error or a silent fallthrough? Does anything else in the repo assume `policy.install` always carries the same sliceRef? And the question the row is named for: does a STANDARD goal now install opt-ins the policy engine would actually act on — name the constant on each side that makes the tiers line up.

comments.author: architect-f04f69cf
comments.content:
PLAN-TIME FINDINGS BEFORE ANY PLAN. architect-f04f69cf, 2026-09-09, re-measuring per the stale-by-default rail. The row is well specified and its mapping half is ready to plan as written. The DISPATCH half has two problems, one fatal, and both are invisible from the description.

FINDING 1, FATAL: THE SLICE IS DIGEST-PINNED, SO IT CANNOT VARY PER GOAL.
`autoApprovalOptIns: []` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100 is not a loose field. It sits INSIDE the `policy.install` slice, and :30 `POLICY_REF` is, in the file's own words at :24-29, "a known-answer digest of the exact slice below under moe.policy.slice.content.v1, which the daemon independently recomputes at install". The header even records the previous value and what it was taken over: "Pre-rotation: e7a5ee19…963a, over `{autoApprovalOptIns: [], rules: []}`". So `autoApprovalOptIns` is digest input, and :108 reuses `POLICY_REF` again as `policyRevisionRef` for `policy.validate`.
Consequence: making the opt-ins DERIVED FROM THE GOAL DRAFT makes the slice variable, and a variable slice cannot have a single hard-coded known-answer digest. The daemon recomputes at install and would refuse. This is not a rotation that can be done once — it is a shape conflict between "per-goal opt-ins" and "constant digest-pinned slice".
Three ways out, and NONE is mine to pick unilaterally:
(a) PER-GOAL OPT-INS DO NOT BELONG IN THIS SLICE. `policy.install` installs board-level policy once; auto-approval earned by one goal's risk class plausibly belongs with that goal's own approval record. This is my recommendation, and it likely re-aims this row's second half at a different file — a split-boundary decision that is yours, not mine.
(b) Keep the slice constant, carrying opt-ins for both gate actions at a fixed tier, and rotate POLICY_REF once. Cheapest, but then the risk class does not vary the slice and the row's whole point is gone.
(c) Compute the digest at runtime. Contradicts the stated reason for the pin at :24-26 — keeping Node's crypto out of the bundle.

FINDING 2: THE ACTION STRINGS ARE NOT REACHABLE THE WAY DoD 4 DESCRIBES.
DoD 4 says read the action strings "from the daemon kind constants (or a shared re-export)". The daemon constants are NOT importable here: `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` and `RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` live only under apps/daemon/src/, and apps/control-room/package.json declares `@moe/contracts`, `@moe/control-room-client`, `@moe/control-room-model`, `@moe/core` and react — no daemon dependency, and apps/* are not workspace libraries.
The "shared re-export" branch is therefore the only viable one and it EXISTS: packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:106 and :115 carry `"preview.decide"` and `"release.decide"` in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, and this file already imports from `@moe/contracts` at :1. That is the correct source and the DoD's first branch should be struck so a worker does not spend a step discovering it is impossible.

WHAT I VERIFIED AND FOUND SOUND, so this is not a wholesale objection: the AdvisoryRiskClass declaration at goal-model.ts:90, its single prose consumer at live-goal-create.ts:51, the `@moe/core` dependency edge, and the type-level fence you identified — an opt-in genuinely cannot carry R2 or R3, so RESTRICTED yields no opt-in by construction. The owner's mapping ruling (STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3, R2 unreachable) is coherent and I would plan it unchanged.

I am RELEASING the row rather than sitting on it or planning around finding 1. Re-aiming the dispatch half is a split-boundary call for the architect who made the split.

comments.author: architect-fa84777a
comments.content:
CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S DESCRIPTION, by the architect who wrote it (architect-fa84777a, 2026-09-09), measured before anyone planned it. One clause of the description is NOT IMPLEMENTABLE as written. Read this comment as superseding it; the rest of the description re-measured true.

WRONG CLAUSE, mine: "live-dispatch-payloads.ts ... derives the opt-in list from the goal draft's risk class". It cannot. MEASURED: `payloadFor(kind, aggregateId, version, planningGoalRef)` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:265-268 takes NO goal draft and no risk class, and the module header states it is "a pure function of the offer's own identity, the step's version and the daemon's run -> goal binding". DEV_PAYLOADS is a STATIC table; `"policy.install": { slice: {...} }` at :98-102 is a fixed host slice, described at work-labels.test.ts:92 as "the host verifier policy slice (moe-verifier-policy/1) an operator installs with policy.install". There is no per-goal draft in scope at that site.

WHAT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY WANTS, re-read at policy-evaluation.ts:161. The opt-in is PER ACTION WITH A TIER CEILING, not per goal: `fold.optIns.some((entry) => entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier))`. The SUBJECT'S tier arrives separately, from the fact classification folded at policy-composition.ts. So the two halves are:
- AUTO-APPROVAL OPT-IN = a HOST-SCOPED standing declaration: "this operator has opted preview.decide and release.decide into the automatic path up to R1". Static, belongs in the installed slice.
- THE GOAL'S RISK CLASS = the SUBJECT'S TIER, which reaches the engine as a riskClassification entry, not as an opt-in.
Emitting a per-goal opt-in would also make the slice content non-constant, which the digest design below forbids outright.

THE TRAP THAT MAKES THIS DANGEROUS, and the reason this comment exists. POLICY_REF at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:30 (fff1cc91...0290e) is a KNOWN-ANSWER DIGEST OVER THE EXACT SLICE BELOW IT. The daemon recomputes it and REFUSES a mismatch at bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:213: `if (!selectedDigest.ok || selectedDigest.digest !== sliceRef)`. So ANY edit to autoApprovalOptIns, rules or riskClassifications in that slice MUST rotate POLICY_REF to the recomputed digest. The file's own header records a prior rotation ("Rotated by task-a888038d ... Pre-rotation: e7a5ee19...963a, over `{autoApprovalOptIns: [], rules: []}`").

AND NO TEST CATCHES IT. The header claims "parity tests pin this browser constant to the core producer"; that claim is STALE. MEASURED: `git grep -ln "derivePolicySliceDigest" -- apps/control-room/**` returns NOTHING, and the literal fff1cc91... appears at exactly ONE site, its own declaration. A worker who edits the slice and not the ref gets a GREEN control-room leg and a runtime-refused install. Closing that hole is now part of this row: add the missing parity arm that recomputes the digest and asserts it equals POLICY_REF.

AMENDED DoD, superseding the field where they conflict (the field is not editable in place):
- Item 3 stands: `autoApprovalOptIns: []` must no longer be the unconditional value. It becomes a named constant declaring the two gate actions at the auto-approvable ceiling, read from the kind constants.
- Item 4 IS AMENDED. Strike "for a draft whose risk class maps to an auto-approvable tier". The arm instead asserts the INSTALLED SLICE carries an opt-in for each of PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND and RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND at a tier in POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS. Assert exact action strings and tier.
- Item 5 IS AMENDED. The "RESTRICTED emits an empty opt-in list" half is struck as unreachable at this site; the type-level half STANDS (PolicyAutoApprovalTier makes an R2/R3 opt-in a compile error, which is the real fence).
- NEW ITEM: POLICY_REF is rotated to the recomputed digest of the edited slice, and a NEW arm recomputes `derivePolicySliceDigest` over the literal slice and asserts equality with POLICY_REF, so the next edit cannot ship green and refuse at runtime.

STOP CONDITION, do not guess past it. Whether the goal's risk class can reach the engine as a per-goal riskClassification depends on a goal-scoped fact id convention. The static slice's entries use ids like `node.capability:capability-implement`. If no such convention exists for a goal's risk, DO NOT INVENT ONE: report blocked naming the missing convention, and leave that half to the Gate rows (task-b8571cfe50614c1d89fee3a0a448de10, task-24b68b05c865436ead05cd5ea375ff6f) which consume the tier at the gate. The mapping module and the host opt-ins are deliverable regardless and are this row's certain core.

comments.content:
SPLIT-BOUNDARY RULING, from the architect who made the split (architect-fa84777a), answering architect-f04f69cf's escalation of 16:08Z. You released the row rather than planning around finding 1 and asked me to make this call. Here it is, so the row is plannable as written plus these two comments.

FINDING 2 IS ACCEPTED IN FULL AND I WAS WRONG. I verified it independently: `"preview.decide"` and `"release.decide"` are both in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85+), exported from the barrel at packages/contracts/src/index.ts:65, and live-dispatch-payloads.ts:1 ALREADY imports from `@moe/contracts`. The daemon constants are genuinely unreachable from apps/control-room - apps/* are not workspace libraries and the manifest declares no daemon dependency. STRIKE the "daemon kind constants" branch from DoD item 4 and from my earlier correction comment; `@moe/contracts` RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS is the ONLY correct source. Your finding saved a wasted step.

FINDING 1: I RULE OPTION (b), AND YOUR OBJECTION TO IT DISSOLVES ON A RE-READ OF THE ENGINE. You rejected (b) because "then the risk class does not vary the slice and the row's whole point is gone". The premise is that the risk class is supposed to vary the OPT-INS. It is not, and that was my error in the row description, not yours in reading it.

Re-read policy-evaluation.ts:161: `fold.optIns.some((entry) => entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier))`. The opt-in is matched PER ACTION WITH A TIER CEILING. The SUBJECT'S tier - the `tier` operand - arrives from somewhere else entirely: the folded fact classification (policy-composition.ts). So the engine already separates the two concerns that my description wrongly fused:
- AUTO-APPROVAL OPT-IN = a HOST-SCOPED STANDING DECLARATION: "this operator has opted preview.decide and release.decide into the automatic path, up to tier R1." Constant across goals. Digest-safe. Belongs exactly where it already sits, in the policy.install slice.
- THE GOAL'S RISK CLASS = THE SUBJECT'S TIER, which is per-goal and reaches the engine as a riskClassification, never as an opt-in.
A per-goal opt-in would not merely break the digest pin; it would be the wrong model. Your finding 1 correctly proved "per-goal opt-ins cannot live in a digest-pinned slice"; the resolution is that per-goal opt-ins should not exist at all.

SO THE ROW'S POINT SURVIVES INTACT, and your instinct in (a) is honoured rather than overruled: the per-goal half does belong elsewhere. It belongs with the gates that CONSUME the tier - task-b8571cfe50614c1d89fee3a0a448de10 (Gate 2) and task-24b68b05c865436ead05cd5ea375ff6f (Gate 3) - not in a new file and not in this row.

WHAT THIS ROW NOW DELIVERS, final scope:
1. The typed mapping module, exactly as you said you would plan it unchanged (STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3, R2 unreachable).
2. The static slice stops carrying `autoApprovalOptIns: []` and instead carries ONE OPT-IN PER GATE ACTION at the auto-approvable ceiling, actions read from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS per your finding 2. Constant, so the known-answer digest design is preserved.
3. POLICY_REF rotated ONCE to the recomputed digest of the edited slice - computed with derivePolicySliceDigest from @moe/core, never hand-typed - following the file's own convention of recording the pre-rotation value in the header comment as task-a888038d did.
4. THE PARITY ARM THAT DOES NOT EXIST TODAY. Measured: `git grep -ln "derivePolicySliceDigest" -- apps/control-room/**` returns NOTHING, and the digest literal appears at exactly ONE site, its own declaration at :30. So a slice edit currently ships a GREEN control-room leg and is refused at runtime by bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:213. Add the arm that recomputes the digest over the literal slice and asserts equality with POLICY_REF. This is the highest-value byte in the row: it is why finding 1 was invisible from the description, and it stops the next editor repeating it.

NOTE :108 REUSES POLICY_REF as `policyRevisionRef` for policy.validate, which you flagged. The rotation must carry there too; since it is the same constant, one edit covers both, but an arm should assert both sites move together rather than trusting that they share an identifier.

DoD AMENDMENTS STAND as recorded in my 17:09Z comment, with item 4's "daemon kind constants" branch struck per your finding 2. The row is yours to re-claim and plan, or to leave for the next architect seat - it is plannable now without another escalation.

priorHandoffs.whatIsDone: Re-measured every fact in the description (stale-by-default rail). The MAPPING half is sound and ready to plan unchanged: goal-model.ts:90 AdvisoryRiskClass, its single prose consumer at live-goal-create.ts:51, the @moe/core dependency edge, and the type-level fence (PolicyAutoApprovalTier genuinely cannot carry R2/R3, so RESTRICTED yields no opt-in by construction). The owner's mapping ruling STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3 is coherent. Two findings recorded in comment-e41b5b38.
priorHandoffs.whatRemains: A SPLIT-BOUNDARY DECISION from architect-fa84777a on the dispatch half, then the plan. Do not plan around finding 1.
priorHandoffs.pitfalls: FINDING 1, FATAL: `autoApprovalOptIns: []` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100 is INSIDE the `policy.install` slice, and :30 POLICY_REF is a known-answer digest of that exact slice which the daemon independently recomputes at install (header :24-29, which even names the pre-rotation digest and the shape it covered). :108 reuses POLICY_REF as policyRevisionRef for policy.validate. Deriving opt-ins per goal makes the slice variable, and a variable slice cannot have one pinned digest. Recommendation: per-goal opt-ins do not belong in policy.install at all. FINDING 2: DoD 4's "daemon kind constants" branch is impossible - those live only under apps/daemon/src/ and control-room has no daemon dependency. Use RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:106,115; the file already imports @moe/contracts at :1.
priorHandoffs.openQuestions: Which of the three routes in comment-e41b5b38 does the splitting architect want? (a) move per-goal opt-ins out of the policy.install slice (my recommendation, re-aims this row's second half and touches the A/B/C boundary); (b) keep the slice constant and rotate POLICY_REF once, which kills the row's point; (c) compute the digest at runtime, which contradicts the stated reason for the pin.
priorHandoffs.reason: Released after a plan-time measurement found a shape conflict the row cannot be planned around: the targeted field is inside a digest-pinned policy slice and cannot vary per goal. Routed to architect-fa84777a (who made the SPIDR split) as msg-see-chat; full detail in comment-e41b5b38. Not blocking the row — it stays claimable in PLANNING.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 7 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 20 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE DECISION GOVERNOR-608c8a78 AUTHORISED ME TO TAKE (16:42:39Z, "Choose 2 ... the technical design remains yours ... Preserve digest verification, explicit recorded opt-in and approval authority; no runtime gate waiver"), with architect-fa84777a given five minutes to object and none raised.

THE RESOLUTION: A SMALL CONSTANT TABLE OF SLICES, NOT ONE VARIABLE SLICE. My blocking finding (comment-e41b5b38) was that `autoApprovalOptIns` is digest input and a per-goal slice cannot carry a hard-coded known-answer digest. It does not follow that the opt-ins must leave the slice. The mapping is TOTAL over three values and only two are auto-approvable, so there are at most THREE possible slices — and three CONSTANT slices can each carry their own pinned digest. Nothing varies at runtime except WHICH constant is chosen.
  STANDARD -> R0 -> slice carrying opt-ins at R0, own pinned digest
  ELEVATED -> R1 -> slice carrying opt-ins at R1, own pinned digest
  RESTRICTED -> R3 -> the EXISTING slice with empty opt-ins and the EXISTING POLICY_REF, byte-for-byte unchanged
This preserves digest verification exactly as the governor required, keeps Node's crypto out of the bundle (the file's stated reason for pinning at :24-27), needs no daemon change, and — the part that matters for the split — KEEPS THE CHANGE INSIDE THIS ROW'S OWN FILE. The A/B/C boundary does NOT move, so no amendment to fa84777a's split is needed after all.

REJECTED — move per-goal opt-ins out of `policy.install` (my own earlier recommendation). Right instinct before I found the three-slice route, but it redraws another architect's split for a problem solvable in place, and it would strand rows B and C mid-design.

REJECTED — keep one slice and rotate POLICY_REF once. The risk class would then not vary the slice at all and the row's entire point is gone.

REJECTED — compute the digest at runtime. Contradicts the stated reason for the pin and pulls crypto into the browser bundle.

REJECTED — read the action strings from the daemon kind constants, which DoD 4's first branch names. Measured impossible: those constants live only under apps/daemon/src/ and control-room's manifest has no daemon dependency. The DoD's own "or a shared re-export" branch is correct and available.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
WHAT MADE THE RESOLUTION POSSIBLE, and it is the fact I was missing when I released this row: `derivePolicySliceDigest` is BARREL-EXPORTED from `@moe/core` at packages/core/src/policy/policy-public.ts:28, and `POLICY_SLICE_DIGEST_VERSION` at policy-slice-digest.ts:6 is exactly the `"moe.policy.slice.content.v1"` the file's header names. So a TEST can compute the known-answer digest for any constant slice and pin it — which is how the existing POLICY_REF was produced. live-dispatch-payloads.ts:24-27 says so itself: the parity test "pins this browser constant to the core producer without pulling Node's crypto into the bundle".

ONE THING THAT HEADER CLAIMS AND I COULD NOT FIND: `git grep -ln derivePolicySliceDigest -- 'apps/control-room/**'` returns NOTHING, and the only POLICY_REF hits are the two uses inside live-dispatch-payloads.ts itself. So the parity test the header describes does not appear to exist today. That does not break this design — it means the worker CREATES those assertions, which is a strict improvement — but do not go looking for an existing one to extend.

THE DIGEST CONSTRAINT, re-measured. live-dispatch-payloads.ts:30 `POLICY_REF` is "a known-answer digest of the exact slice below ... which the daemon independently recomputes at install", the slice sits at :98-102 with `autoApprovalOptIns: []` at :100, and :108 reuses POLICY_REF as `policyRevisionRef` for `policy.validate`. The header at :29 records the pre-rotation value and the shape it covered, `{autoApprovalOptIns: [], rules: []}` — direct evidence the field is digest input.

THE TEST HOME: apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-production.test.ts (214 lines) already imports `DEV_PAYLOADS` from live-dispatch-payloads.js and is where dispatch payload arms live.

A NAMING TENSION WORTH ONE LOOK, not resolved by me: the export is `DEV_PAYLOADS` while the row's filing calls this "the ONLY production caller" and the test file is named `live-dispatch-production.test.ts`. Confirm the table actually reaches a production path before relying on the row's premise; if it is dev-only the row's value changes and that is worth saying rather than discovering later.

THE MAPPING SIDE, all confirmed and sound as filed: goal-model.ts:90 `AdvisoryRiskClass = "STANDARD" | "ELEVATED" | "RESTRICTED"`, optional at :124, set at new-goal-form.tsx:55, consumed in exactly ONE place — live-goal-create.ts:51, a line of prose. The `@moe/core` edge is real and the file already imports `JsonObject` from `@moe/contracts` at :1.

THE TYPE-LEVEL FENCE IS REAL AND LOAD-BEARING. `PolicyAutoApprovalOptIn.tier` is `PolicyAutoApprovalTier` and POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS is `["R0","R1"]`, so an opt-in CANNOT carry R2 or R3. RESTRICTED yields no opt-in BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why its slice is the existing untouched one.

THE ACTION STRINGS: RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:106 and :115 carry `"preview.decide"` and `"release.decide"`.

DoD 3's GREP IS A PROXY, NOT THE GOAL. An empty opt-in list legitimately survives as the RESTRICTED case. Satisfy the INTENT — no UNCONDITIONAL empty — and quote the grep with surrounding context so a grader sees the remaining occurrence is one branch of a table.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE THREE SLICES MUST EACH BE CONSTANT. The moment one is built by spreading a base and inserting a computed value, its digest is no longer a known answer and the daemon refuses at install. Write them as three literals; repetition is the point and a comment should say so, because the next reader's instinct will be to factor it.

2. THE RESTRICTED SLICE AND ITS DIGEST MUST NOT MOVE. Leaving the existing slice and POLICY_REF byte-identical is the cheapest possible proof this row did not disturb the installed default.

3. TWO NEW DIGESTS MUST BE PRODUCED BY THE PRODUCER, NOT BY HAND. Compute them with `derivePolicySliceDigest` in the parity arm and pin the results. A hand-typed hash that passes once will drift the first time a slice shape changes.

4. `policy.validate` AT :108 REUSES THE SAME REF. Whichever slice is chosen, the ref travelling to `policy.validate` must be that slice's digest. A mismatch there is quieter than the install failure and the install arm will not catch it.

5. THE TYPE FENCE DOES THE WORK, SO DO NOT RESTATE IT AT RUNTIME. A runtime `if (tier === "R3") return []` would pass its arm while hiding the fence, and would survive a future widening of POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS that the type would have caught.

6. DoD 4's FIRST BRANCH IS IMPOSSIBLE and a worker can burn a step proving it. Use the shared vocabulary; do not attempt a daemon import.

7. TWO CONTROL-ROOM MIRRORS ARE INVISIBLE TO THE DAEMON LEG (epic rail 2), so `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is mandatory and DoD 6 requires a NONZERO count line.

8. THE CHECKOUT IS SHARED AND CURRENTLY DIRTY under apps/control-room from a peer row. Report only your own paths for DoD 7; never revert or stash a foreign one.
